result.reasoning:
REFUTED on six independent counts. Every load-bearing step of the finding fails under reproduction; only two inert side-facts survive.

R1 — The stated mechanism (sign / centring) is arithmetically wrong. `cutoff = best - rel*abs(best)` (clustering.py:102) gives a survivor band of width `rel*|best|` for BOTH signs: best=+0.0226 -> cutoff +0.0113 (band 0.0113); best=-0.0226 -> cutoff -0.0339 (band 0.0113). Sign-flip test holding the gap structure fixed (v1 section 2): fits [0.0226, 0.0162, 0.0112, 0.0078, 0.0042, 0.0001] -> 2/6 clusters survive; fits [-0.0226, -0.0290, -0.0340, -0.0374, -0.0410, -0.0451] -> 2/6 clusters survive. Identical. The claim "when best is negative the band is 0.5*|best| wide and culls far more than intended" is false; the band is 0.5*|best| wide when best is positive too. The rule is not sign-dependent, it is merely not shift-invariant — and a LARGE negative best keeps everything (best=-3.0226 -> cutoff -4.5339 -> 6/6 survive).

R2 — The premise "written for a fitness bounded below by 0" is false. AlphaCube's own GP fitness is `(base if signed else abs(base)) - turnover_penalty*turnover` (scoring.py:77) with production penalty 0.14 and no clamp (-inf is only the coverage/finite rejection, scoring.py:74-77). |rank_ic| 0.015 with turnover 0.8 gives -0.0970. Simulated production-scale generations give a best cluster mean around -0.0087. The cutoff formula has always run with a best that may be small or negative; Partura introduced no new regime.

R3 — In the observed e1 regime the cull is LESS aggressive than AlphaCube's own, not "far more". 40 real 48-tree populations built with the real `TypedTreeGenerator` and clustered with the real `cluster_population(merge_threshold=0.8)` (~16.8 clusters per generation), fits drawn from e1's recorded scores: raw `0.03*score` keeps 7.70/16.8 = 45.8% of clusters (steer arm) and 14.40/16.8 = 85.6% (control arm). AlphaCube's own `|rank_ic| - 0.14*turnover` on the same clustering keeps 6.80/16.8 = 40.4%. The differenced reward survives MORE culling than AlphaCube's own fitness.

R4 — The 8-singleton arithmetic is not what `cull_clusters` does: it thresholds on cluster MEANS (clustering.py:95-104), and `cluster_population` absorbs singletons into the nearest cluster by operator-family cosine (clustering.py:73-89). Over 60 real 48-tree populations with one `fit == 0.0` injected, the best cluster mean was exactly 0.0 in ZERO of them — the 0.0 tree always landed in a merged cluster of 3-8 members, dragging that cluster's mean negative (mean best cluster mean -0.0284). Resulting cutoffs -0.030 to -0.061, with 3-11 clusters / 3-34 individuals surviving. The "cutoff = 0.0 empties 7 of 8 clusters" result only follows if each individual is its own singleton cluster. With real clustering plus the real e1 score distribution and an injected 0.0, collapse to <=2 surviving individuals occurred in 3/60 (steer) and 6/60 (control) draws.

R5 — The downstream consequence does not follow even when the collapse is forced. Replicating `_next_generation` exactly (gp.py:670-692; elitism=1, crossover_rate=0.7, mutation_rate=0.3, tournament_size=3) with survivors forced to a single cluster, over the 4 generations that budget 192 / population 48 allows (gp.py:735): 33, 66 and 123 distinct new expressions bred across three trials. "the remaining budget produces nothing" is false — mutation and `_mutate`'s `generator.generate()` fallback keep injecting new structure every generation.

R6 — `best == 0.0` is unreachable, so the headline scenario has no live path. `reward()` (steer.py:424-440) maximises train long_sharpe over sign in (+1,-1) x hl in (0, 5, 20); an exactly-zero `long_screen` score needs the candidate to screen nothing at all six combinations. Measured: `z > 0.3` can only be emptied by tying >= ~40% of names at the relevant tail; closing BOTH tails (required for sign=-1) leaves <= 20% distinct names and `distinct_fraction` falls to 0.102-0.203, far under the `dist >= 0.5` gate at idea_search.py:145. The one route preserving distinctness — a candidate finite only where `ctx.base` is NaN — gives 2.0% coverage against `min_coverage=0.9` (idea_search.py:268 -> gp.py:323 -> scoring.py:75), so `self.base.score` returns fit=-inf and `steer_reward` is never called (idea_search.py:141-151). On top of that, `bk.smoothed` at hl 5/20 breaks the ties: even where hl=0 screens 0.00% of cells, hl=5 and hl=20 screen ~20%, so the maximiser always has a non-no-op orientation that beats 0.0. Every engineered no-op in the sweep was either GATED OUT or returned a strictly nonzero score (+1.21, +1.61, +1.87, +2.09).

R7 — The suggested fix is unprincipled and would itself change the numbers. On the same clustering and the same fits: raw -> 45.8%/85.6% of clusters survive; `0.03*(score+3.0)` -> 64.3%/99.7% (and 88.7%/100.0% in the injected-zero run, i.e. culling becomes a no-op); `0.03*(score+1.0)` -> 40.7%/38.3%, i.e. MORE aggressive than raw. The offset is a free parameter that silently re-tunes selection pressure, and a shift-dependent cutoff is still shift-dependent after a shift. The fix also rests on a second false premise — that the level rewards are nonnegative. They are not: `score = min(s_tr, s_va)` of a pure-long Sharpe (steer.py:452-453) is routinely negative for a random candidate, so `long` / `long_tradable` / `long_bucket` straddle zero exactly as the differenced rewards do, and "keeping 0.03 x score for the level rewards" would leave them in the regime the finding claims is broken.

Surviving but inert: (i) `long_marginal` / `long_screen` do return a difference that straddles zero (steer.py:443-453) — true, and the archive confirms all 210 recorded e1 fits are negative (steer -0.0186..-0.0908, control -0.0226..-0.0451); (ii) `gp_params` at idea_search.py:262 does not pass `cull_rel_threshold`, so the 0.5 default is in force — true. Neither produces a wrong number: the measured cull is in the same band as AlphaCube's own fitness, the degenerate cutoff requires a best cluster mean at zero which cannot occur, and the finding's own proposed remedy changes the search's selectivity more than the alleged defect does.

result.corrected_fix:
No change warranted — but if the band is touched at all, do NOT offset the reward.

Why the proposed fix is wrong: an additive constant on `score` is a free parameter that re-tunes GP selection pressure with no principled value. Measured on identical populations and identical fits, `+3.0` raises surviving clusters from 45.8%/85.6% to 64.3%/99.7% (and to 88.7%/100.0% in the injected-zero run, i.e. it disables cluster culling entirely), while `+1.0` lowers them to 40.7%/38.3%. It also cannot be applied only to the differenced rewards as proposed: `score = min(s_tr, s_va)` of a pure-long Sharpe (partura/steer.py:452-453) is routinely negative too, so `long`/`long_tradable`/`long_bucket` straddle zero as well, and "keeping 0.03 x score for the level rewards" would leave them in the regime the finding calls broken. Finally, since `p_score` is already recorded unchanged (idea_search.py:159) and the THR gate reads `score_p_score` from the checkpoint (idea_search.py:284-288), an offset buys nothing for the gate — it only perturbs selection.

If the team nevertheless wants the band made explicit rather than inherited, the only correct Partura-side lever is the one the finding dismissed: set it openly in `gp_params` at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py:262, e.g. `gp = dict(..., cull_rel_threshold=0.5)`, so the value is recorded in the episode rather than silently defaulted — paired with logging the per-generation `best` cluster mean so the band width is auditable. A genuinely shift-invariant rule would have to replace the relative cutoff with a spread-based one (for example a cutoff at a fixed quantile of the cluster means, or `best - rel * (best - median(means))`), and that lives in /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/mining/clustering.py:102, which is read-only here and whose current behaviour was measured to be no more aggressive under Partura's reward (45.8%/85.6% surviving) than under AlphaCube's own fitness (40.4%).
